references.text: God promised Moses that He would teach him what to say: 'Go now! I will be with your mouth and teach you what you shall speak.' This is an early promise of divine guidance in speech, parallel to Jesus' promise that the Holy Spirit will teach the disciples what they should say. [ref:Ex 4:12|Exodus 4:12]

God told Jeremiah not to fear, for God would put His words in his mouth: 'Everything I command you, you shall speak.' This shows the same pattern of God giving His servants the words they need at the right time. [ref:Jer 1:7-9|Jeremiah 1:7-9]

Jesus tells the disciples that when they are handed over to authorities, they should not worry about what to say, for it will be given to them in that very hour what they ought to speak. 'For it is not you who speak, but your Father's Spirit speaking through you.' This is a close parallel in Matthew to the promise in Luke 12:12. [ref:Matt 10:19-20|Matthew 10:19-20]

Mark's version of the same promise: 'When they lead you away and hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what to say; but whatever is given to you in that hour, speak it. For it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.' [ref:Mark 13:11|Mark 13:11]

Later in Luke's Gospel, Jesus repeats this promise in an eschatological context: 'So make up your minds not to prepare beforehand how to defend yourselves. For I will give you words and wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to resist or contradict.' [ref:Luke 21:14-15|Luke 21:14-15]

Jesus promises that the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, will teach the disciples all things and remind them of everything He has said. This expands on the promise in Luke 12:12 regarding the Spirit's teaching role. [ref:John 14:26|John 14:26]

Jesus promises that the Spirit of truth will guide the disciples into all truth and speak what He hears. This is further elaboration on the Spirit's role as guide and teacher. [ref:John 16:13|John 16:13]

The fulfillment of Jesus' promise: Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, speaks boldly before the Council and defends himself with words given to him by the Spirit, just as Jesus had promised. [ref:Acts 4:8-10|Acts 4:8-10]

Stephen spoke with a wisdom and Spirit that his opponents could not resist. This is a concrete fulfillment of the promise that the Holy Spirit would give the disciples what they should say. [ref:Acts 6:10|Acts 6:10]

Paul writes that they speak in words taught by the Spirit, not in words taught by human wisdom. This aligns with the promise that the Holy Spirit will teach believers what to say. [ref:1 Cor 2:13|1 Corinthians 2:13]
